rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: The phrase is glossed as God having given people something of everything they need.
rows.anchor: (وأوتيت من كل شيء) عن الأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that someone among people has asked for each kind of thing, so God gave from what they asked.
rows.anchor: ليس شيء إلا وقد سأله بعض الناس، فقال تعالى

rows.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: An alternative says God gave people things they never asked Him for.
rows.anchor: أعطاكم ما لم تسألوه، عن الضحاك، وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that some requests go unanswered is answered by the partitive min: God grants according to what is beneficial and in its proper time.
rows.anchor: لذلك أدخل (من) وهي للتبعيض فيعطي بحسب المصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the informed petitioner who asks for what is beneficial counts; an ignorant person's request need not be considered.
rows.anchor: إنما المعتبر بسؤال العارف الذي يسأل بشرط المصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's blessings cannot be counted because they are numerous and include visible and unknown benefits: bodily, provision, worldly, religious, and averting calamities.
rows.anchor: لأن أنواع النعم في بدنه ورزقه ومنافعه دنيا ثم منافع الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes God as benefactor and thus the one deserving worship; “human” here means disbelievers rather than humanity universally.
rows.anchor: فبين أنه المنعم وأنه المستحق للعبادة لكن الإنسان مع هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss calls the disbeliever unjust to himself through ingratitude toward his Lord and consequent deserving of punishment.
rows.anchor: ظلوم لنفسه بما كفر من نعم ربه واستوجب العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss calls him unjust to blessings because he attributes them to someone other than their originator, and intensely ungrateful.
rows.anchor: ظلوم للنعم حيث أضافها إلى غير مبتدئها كفار مبالغة في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation contrasts injustice in hardship with ingratitude in prosperity.
rows.anchor: ظلوم في الشدة، كفار في النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legal implication is that believers should hasten to obedience, including establishing prayer and giving alms.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على وجوب المبادرة إلى الطاعات من إقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous deeds are best for the accountable because God commands them, promises reward for them, and threatens punishment for their omission.
rows.anchor: لأنها أصلح الأعمال للمكلف من حيث أمر بها ووعد الثواب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Better reward” means the best recompense for an act, and “better hope” means the best object one may hope for; false hopes lead to ruin.
rows.anchor: خير جزاء على العمل وخير أملا أي: خير شيء يأمله المرء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges seeking Paradise and detachment from the world by recalling its swift passing and short duration.
rows.anchor: الحث على طلب الجنة ونعيمها، والزهد في الدنيا من حيث نبه على سرعة فنائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is compared either to water, which does not settle or remain unchanged and may help or harm, or to a briefly beautiful plant that dries, yellows, crumbles, and vanishes in the wind.
rows.anchor: شبه بالماء من حيث لا يستقر في موضع ولا يبقى على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imagined question asks why people were not given enough to worship without needing to earn; the answer is that livelihood is a trial, examination, and kindness that prompts reflection.
rows.anchor: فجوابنا: ابتلاء وامتحانا ولطفا لهم، ليتدبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earning is itself a kind of worship; it humbles people, and their mutual need teaches them that God alone is self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: ولأن الكسب نوع عبادة، ولأنه تصغير أحواله لعلمه أنه تعالى قادر حي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preceding question about divine istiwāʾ, the author says the sounder view of Abū ʿAlī is that it means power; the Kullābī account of an act or attribute called istiwāʾ is unintelligible.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الأصح ما ذهب إليه أبو علي أن المراد به الاقتدار

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamzah reads the hāʾ of “for his family” with ḍamma by transferring the hamzah’s vowel; the others read it with kasra for two adjacent sukūns.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة: لأهله امكثوا بضم الهاء، نقل حركة الهمزة إلى الهاء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read “annī” with fatḥa, understood as “because I am your Lord”; the others use kasra as the beginning of a new quotation, “he said: I am.”
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو: ياموسى أني أنا ربك بفتح الألف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers open the final yāʾ in “innī”; the remaining readers leave it quiescent.
rows.anchor: فأما الياء ففتحها أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read Ṭuwā with ḍamma and no tanwīn; another group uses ḍamma with tanwīn, while a reading reported from Abū ʿAmr has kasra without declension, treating it as a place-name.
rows.anchor: في طوى ثلاث قراءات: الأولى: بضم الطاء غير منون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No tanwīn may reflect a place-name or a form altered from Ṭāwin; tanwīn reflects masculine treatment and lightening, and readers differ between tafkhīm and imāla because of the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: أما ترك الإجراء لأنه اسم البقعة أو هو معدول من طاو

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamzah intensifies “anā” and reads “ikhtarnāka” with nūn and alif for magnification; the others read “ikhtartuka” with singular tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة (أنا) بالتشديد. (اخترناك) بالنون والألف على التفخيم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن
rows.claim: They read “ukhfīhā” with fatḥa on the alif, giving the sense “I reveal it”; the common reading has ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير والحسن: أخفيها بفتح الألف أي: أظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Play and amusement are defects and cannot be ascribed to God; play or absurdity is unproductive activity like children's play.
rows.anchor: واللعب والعبث من النظائر، وهو كل عمل لا يجدي نفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zāhiq can mean one that perishes, but also a fat or stout animal; “his soul departed” is another usage.
rows.anchor: والزاهق من الأضداد، يقال للهالك زاهق، والسمين من الدواب زاهق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lahw is anything that occupies or distracts; the accompanying report says that when God takes something for Himself, one should turn away from it.
rows.anchor: واللهو معروف، وكل ما شغلك فقد ألهاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damag means striking the head through to the brain, and by extension destroying; the Prophet is described as the breaker of hosts of falsehood.
rows.anchor: والدمغ: شج الرأس حتى يبلغ الدماغ، يقال: دمغه يدمغه دمغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istihsār means exhaustion and loss of strength; its root image is uncovering one's arms and using up one's power through fatigue.
rows.anchor: والاستحسار: الانقطاع من الإعياء، يقال: بعير حسير إذا أعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also describes distant-sight fatigue and an unarmored soldier; ḥāsir is one who has uncovered himself by lacking armor.
rows.anchor: والحاسر في الحرب: الذي لا درع له ولا مغفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Futūr is weakness; a report distinguishes an intoxicant that removes reason from a muffling substance that weakens the body, and Ibn al-Aʿrābī describes a man as weakened in his limbs and gaze.
rows.anchor: نهى عن كل مسكر ومفتر فالمسكر ما يزيل العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth is distinguished from falsehood by proofs, which makes the image of casting truth onto falsehood appropriate.
rows.anchor: هاتوا برهانكم أي: حجتكم على ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The question about earthly gods links to the command to ask the People of the Reminder: ask whether messengers were ever other than men and whether earthly idols can create; all messengers called to God's oneness.
rows.anchor: إنه يتصل بقوله: (فاسألوا أهل الذكر) أي: سلهم هل أرسل قبلك إلا رجالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another coherence reading connects the claim about taking amusement to the opponents' attribution of a child and partner to God.
rows.anchor: يتصل بقوله: (لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا) أي: أضافوا إليه الولد

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The question that God is not questioned about His acts connects to the approaching reckoning: people will be asked whether they thanked or rejected His blessings.
rows.anchor: إنه يتصل بقوله: (اقترب للناس حسابهم) والحساب هو السؤال عما أنعم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse follows the preceding proof by adding divine justice to the discussion of unity.
rows.anchor: يتصل بما قبله؛ لأنه بين التوحيد وعطفه عليه ببيان العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This is a reminder of those with me and before me” can refer back to the preceding discussion of unity and justice in the Qur'an and earlier scriptures; the author prefers this connection over treating it as a fresh start.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو استئناف، والوجه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's acts are all wisdom and right, so no one asks why He did what is right.
rows.anchor: جميع أفعاله حكمة وصواب، ولا يقال: لم فعلت الصواب

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: No one can demand an account from God for blessings; rather, He asks everyone whether they were grateful or ungrateful for His gifts.
rows.anchor: له النعم على جميعهم فيسألهم عنها شكروا أم كفروا، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: A true deity cannot be questioned, while the Messiah and angels would be questioned; their accountability proves they are servants, not gods.
rows.anchor: وكان يجب ألا يسأل المسيح والملائكة، فلما كان من حقه أن يسألهم دل أنهم عبيد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God is above all things and can question them, whereas nothing is above Him to question Him.
rows.anchor: لأنه فوق الأشياء فيسألهم، ولا شيء فوقه فيسأله، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remembrance is the Qur'an and other revealed books, which teach monotheism and justice.
rows.anchor: ما تقدم ذكره من التوحيد والعدل مذكور في القرآن وسائر الكتب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: “This is a reminder of those with me and before me” refers to earlier communities, some saved through faith and others destroyed for disbelief.
rows.anchor: من الأمم ممن نجا بالإيمان أو هلك بالكفر، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The present reminder is the Qur'an's affirmation of exclusive divinity, while the earlier reminder is in the Torah and Gospel; each book recounts its own community.
rows.anchor: هذا ذكر من معي بالحق في إخلاص الإلهية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view identifies both the current and prior reminder with the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: من القرآن ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the verse describes the Prophet's contemporary polytheists and those before them, whose claims have no proof.
rows.anchor: هذا ذكر المشركين الذين في عصر نبينا والذين كانوا قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation includes contemporary believers and scholars and earlier prophets and scholars; most reject reflection and turn away from truth, the Qur'an, or the Prophet, though some believe.
rows.anchor: هذا ذكر من معي من المؤمنين والعلماء، وذكر من قبلي من الأنبياء وعلماء الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every messenger was sent to call people to God's oneness and worship; those who depart from this have neither rational nor revealed warrant.
rows.anchor: لم نبعث رسولا إلا دعا إلى التوحيد وأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deity must be able to give life, cause death, and originate creation; beings lacking these powers cannot rightly be worshipped.
rows.anchor: من حق المعبود أن يقدر على الإحياء والإماتة وعلى الاختراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument that multiple governors would bring disorder establishes divine unity: opposing wills would seek contradictory outcomes, which cannot both occur.
rows.anchor: لو كان فيهما مدبران لفسد الأمر بأن يريد أحدهما ضد ما يريد الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the dualist claim that two eternal beings may differ as one capable and the other incapable, sharing eternity entails likeness in essential attributes; otherwise differing actions would also undermine their shared eternality.
rows.anchor: الاشتراك في القدم يوجب التماثل في سائر صفات النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that both deities will the same things fails because each may will a contrary outcome, such as motion versus rest, and it confuses one agent with two.
rows.anchor: يفعل هذا إرادة التحريك والآخر التسكين، ولأن هذا يؤدي إلى التباس القادر بالقادرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that the deities never oppose one another because each wills what is wise misses the argument: the possibility of opposition shows one has limited power and is not divine.
rows.anchor: كلامنا يجري بصحة التمانع لا بوقوع التمانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that possible injustice does not prove ignorance is answered by distinguishing it from actual injustice; for the proof of unity, possible and actual mutual opposition equally show one deity is more powerful.
rows.anchor: صحة التمانع ووجوده سواء في دلالة أن أحدهما أقدر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Grammatically, “that” is an object of “calls” and functions like a relative pronoun; the phrase about the one whose harm is nearer begins a new clause, or “that” may be nominative with “a wretched protector” as its predicate.
rows.anchor: وموضع (ذلك) نصب ب (يدعو)، وهو بمعنى (الذي)، كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The occasion is a migrant who prospered in health, family, and livestock and praised Islam, but called it bad when illness, a daughter, financial loss, or delayed charity came.
rows.anchor: فنزلت الآية: (ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف)، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma asked the Prophet for gifts, praising Islam when given them and threatening to return to polytheism if refused.
rows.anchor: نزلت في بني أسد بن خزيمة جاءوا إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī identifies the people as hypocrites who praise religion at one time and condemn it at another.
rows.anchor: نزلت في المنافقين، عن أبي علي؛ لأنه يمدح الدين في وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative identifies weak Muslims, who may apostatize, unlike hypocrites who were always disbelievers; another says the hypocrite's alternating praise and blame is like turning over.
rows.anchor: نزلت في ضعفة المسلمين؛ لأن المسلم يكون منقلبا على وجهه بالارتداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another occasion for “whoever thinks” concerns Asad and Ghaṭafān, who hesitated to accept Islam because victory by Muhammad might break their alliance with the Jews and stop their provisions.
rows.anchor: نزل قوله: (من كان يظن) في أسد وغطفان، تثاقلوا عن الإسلام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: “On an edge” means worship on a doubtful, unsteady footing; it can also mean a weak or marginal religious commitment.
rows.anchor: على ضعف في العبادة كضعف القيام على حرف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the edge is worship by tongue without heart: religion has two parts, tongue and heart, and confession unsupported by the heart is precarious.
rows.anchor: الدين حرفان: أحدهما اللسان، والثاني القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When worldly good arrives, such a person settles into the religion; when bodily or financial hardship comes, he reverts to disbelief and loses both worlds.
rows.anchor: فإن أصابه خير أي: صحة في بدنه وسعة في معيشته اطمأن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The powerless objects are idols; alternatively, obedience to them brings no benefit and disobedience brings no harm. The worshipper turns to idols or leaders whose harm is nearer than their benefit.
rows.anchor: يعني الأوثان لا تنفع ولا تضر، وقيل: لا ينفعه إن أطاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If someone sees a wrong but cannot change it, the least duty of enjoining right and forbidding wrong is to disapprove of it inwardly.
rows.anchor: ينكره بقلبه، وهو أقل أحوال الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read “aṣḥāb layka” with an unhamzated name of a city, treated as a definite non-declinable proper noun; others read “al-aykah,” with two spellings viewed as dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر: (أصحاب ليكة) مفتوحة اللام والياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aykah is a thicket or any place of densely interwoven trees; layka and aykah are two Arabic forms.
rows.anchor: والليكة والأيكة لغتان، وأيك جمع أيكة وهي الغيضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iyfāʾ means giving the full due without shortfall; a mukhsir causes a loss by reducing capital, the opposite of increasing it.
rows.anchor: الإيفاء: إعطاء الواجب بكماله من غير نقصان، أوفى يوفي إيفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qisṭās is just measurement by volume; its association with Greek is rejected because the Qur'an is Arabic, so the word is either Arabized or shared across languages.
rows.anchor: والقسطاس: العدل في التقويم على المقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijārah is a contract exchanging use or services for compensation, and is permissible in Islamic law as it was in the earlier community's law.
rows.anchor: وهي عقد على منافع بعوض، وهو جائز في شريعتنا، كما جاز في شريعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwa and qudra are near-synonyms; the root of strength evokes the tightly twisted strands of a rope, then came to mean power.
rows.anchor: وأصل القوة: شدة الفتل من قوى الحبل وهي طاقاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amānah is the opposite of betrayal and means delivering what one is obligated to deliver.
rows.anchor: والأمانة: نقيض الخيانة، وهو أداء ما يجب أداؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nikāḥ is used for intercourse and for the marriage contract; the sounder legal view is that it literally denotes the contract, possibly through transfer from its figurative linguistic use.
rows.anchor: والأصح أنه في عرف الشرع حقيقة للعقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥujjah is a year, and ajal means a span or appointed time.
rows.anchor: والحجج: جمع حجة، وهي السنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īnās means seeing something that feels familiar or reassuring; a jadhwah is a thick piece of wood with fire, like the root of a tree.
rows.anchor: والجذوة: الغليظة من الحطب فيها النار، وهي مثل الجذوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fixed appointed term delays an otherwise imminent annihilating punishment; this refutes the claim that God must preserve people because their continued life benefits others.
rows.anchor: فيبطل قول أصحاب الأصلح أن التبقية واجبة لهذه العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Taste” indicates that punishment is deserved because of people's own deeds, which originate from them, contrary to the Jabriyya on both points.
rows.anchor: العذاب يستحق بعملهم، وأن أعمالهم حادثة من جهتهم، خلاف قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم
rows.claim: They open the yāʾ in “my servants”; the others leave it unvocalized, and all preserve the yāʾ at a pause because it appears in every codex.
rows.anchor: كلهم يقفون عليه بالياء وإثباتها من فتح ومن لم يفتح

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads the conjunction with fatḥa in “my earth is spacious.”
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر أن من قوله: (إن أرضي واسعة) ولم يفتحها غيره

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: In one transmission, ʿĀṣim reads “you are returned” with yāʾ referring to everyone; the other readers use the second-person tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم في بعض الروايات عنه: يرجعون بالياء إلى الكل

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read “lanuthwiyannahum” with thāʾ, meaning to lodge them; the others read “lanubawwiʾannahum” with bāʾ, meaning to settle them in a dwelling.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: لنثوينهم بالثاء من أثويته منزلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabawwuʾ is taking a home or refuge, with a root sense of returning, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: [والتبوء]: اتخاذ منزل يأوي إليه، وأصله: الرجوع، ومنه: (وباءو بغضب)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in “worship Me” may mark the consequence: if a place constrains you, worship God elsewhere because His earth is wide.
rows.anchor: الفاء في قوله: [(فاعبدون)] قيل: دخل للجزاء تقديره: إن ضاق بكم موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Me” is the object of an implied verb interpreted by the following command to worship.
rows.anchor: (إياي) منصوب بمضمر تفسيره ما بعده، وهو قوله: [(فاعبدون)]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tasting death” is read in the genitive construction, though a non-construct reading is also possible; “ka-ʾayyin” means “how many.”
rows.anchor: (ذائقة الموت) جر على الإضافة، ويجوز لغير الإضافة

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: The command to emigrate was revealed for believers in Mecca who were too weak to make their faith public.
rows.anchor: في المستضعفين من المؤمنين كانوا بمكة، ولا يقدرون على إظهار الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision verse was revealed about people persecuted by polytheists who hesitated to migrate because they had no home or property in Medina and feared hunger and thirst.
rows.anchor: كيف نخرج إلى المدينة وليس لنا بها دار ولا عقار، فمن يطعمنا ويسقينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither residence nor provision excuses abandoning obedience: where religious practice is impossible, believers should migrate so they are not put to trial.
rows.anchor: إذا كانوا في بلد لا يلتئم لهم أمر دينهم أن ينقلوا إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: One view is that believers should leave a place where God's command is disobeyed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إذا عمل في أمري بالمعصية فاخرجوا منها إن أرضي واسعة، عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Another view says to flee when ordered to commit sins because the earth is spacious.
rows.anchor: إذا أمرتم بالمعاصي فاهربوا فإن أرضي واسعة، عن عطاء، ومجاهد، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: مطرف
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the earth's spaciousness as the breadth of its provision.
rows.anchor: أرضي واسعة بما أخرج منها من الرزق لكم، عن مطرف

rows.speaker: أبو علي وجماعة
rows.claim: Another interpretation understands God's spacious earth as Paradise, which worshippers should seek; most commentators instead take it as the earthly world.
rows.anchor: أرضي واسعة أي: أرض الجنة فاعبدوني لتنالوها، عن أبي علي وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every living person dies wherever they are, so believers should not remain in a land of polytheism; they return to God for resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: كل حي يموت يناله الموت بأي أرض كان، فلا تقيموا بأرض الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this teaches that the world is a transient waystation and should not be preferred over the everlasting abode of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: دار الدنيا دار نقلة، فلا نختارها على دار الآخرة

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read “lā yanfaʿ” with a masculine verb referring to the excuse; the others use a feminine verb to agree with the word “excuse,” the first following meaning and the second the wording.
rows.anchor: (لا ينفع) بالياء للعذر، وقرأ الباقون بالتاء لقوله تعالى: (معذرتهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labth and mukth are near-synonyms, but labth entails a place, unlike mere continuance; one says God is abiding, not dwelling in a place.
rows.anchor: البقاء لا يتضمنه، لذلك يقال: الله تعالى باق، ولا يقال: لابث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maʿdhirah is an explanation that removes blame, and can also mean the excuse itself.
rows.anchor: والمعذرة: إظهار ما يسقط اللائمة، وهو العذر أيضا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl explains ʿitāb as reproach or a chastising conversation, while iʿtāb is a return to the displeased person's favor and istiʿtāb is seeking that reconciliation.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل: المعاتبة: مخاطبة الإذلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istikhfāf is seeking lightness; to make a people light is to prompt them to act hastily, and being overcome by delight removes good judgment.
rows.anchor: والاستخفاف: طلب الخفة، واستخف قومه: حملهم على الخفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Faith” is parsed either as coordinated with knowledge or as accusative after deleting the preposition maʿ; “in God's book” can mean by His book or written in it.
rows.anchor: نصب (الإيمان) قيل: عطفا على العلم، وقيل: بنزع الخافض

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: “You remained in the Book of God” may mean in God's decree, the Preserved Tablet, or as God announced in His scripture.
rows.anchor: في حكم الله وما كتبه عليه، وقيل: في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the statement as: you remained until the appointed Day of Resurrection promised in God's book, where “book” means a decree or obligation.
rows.anchor: لبثتم إلى يوم البعث الذي وعدتم في كتاب الله، أي: في الأجل الذي سماه وأوجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reverses the syntax to “those endowed with knowledge of God's book and faith”; the learned correct people who thought acknowledgment of a short duration would postpone punishment.
rows.anchor: ظنوا أن العذاب يتأخر عنهم إذا اعترفوا بمدة قليلة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr has several transmitted vocalizations for “my son”; the author identifies one as the relied-upon set and notes the many variants.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن كثير في مثل ذلك آثار جمة، والمعتمد ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ opens the yāʾ of “my son” throughout the Qur'an; the other readers use kasra. Sukun follows the original form, fatḥa drops the possessive after three yāʾs, and kasra is close to the possessive form.
rows.anchor: أما السكون: فلأنه الأصل كما لو وقف، وأما الفتح: فعلى حذف الإضافة

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads “his weaning” without the alif; the other readers use the form with alif.
rows.anchor: وقراءة القراء: (فصاله) بالألف، وعن يعقوب: (فصله) بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahn means weakness.
rows.anchor: الوهن: الضعف، ومنه: (ولا تهنوا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiṣāl means weaning, named for cutting the child off from the maternal breast.
rows.anchor: والفصال: الفطام، وأصله: القطع، فصلت بين الشيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inābah means returning.
rows.anchor: والإنابة: الرجوع، أناب ينيب: إذا رجع

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: “When Luqman said to his son” coordinates with the account of wisdom, as if he was given wisdom when commanded to thank God and when admonishing his son; “while admonishing him” is circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل: آتيناه الحكمة إذ أمرناه بالشكر، وإذ قال لقمان لابنه واعظا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about dutifulness was revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ: his mother swore not to eat until he abandoned his religion, but ate after three days when he would not recant.
rows.anchor: حلفت أمه لا تأكل طعاما حتى تموت، أو يدع دينه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads “the weight of a grain” in the nominative, either as the subject of kāna without a predicate or with kāna treated as inactive; the others use the accusative as its predicate.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع: مثقال حبة بالرفع على أنه اسم (كان)

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read “lā tuṣaʿʿir” without alif; other readers use “tuṣāʿir.” Both prohibit arrogantly turning the cheek away, an image based on a camel-neck disease.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر: (ولا تصعر) بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's line about a tyrant turning his cheek illustrates the metaphor of arrogant disdain.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: وكنا إذا الجبار صعر خده

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read “His blessing” in the plural with a possessive ending; the others read a singular indefinite intended generically, as in 14:34.
rows.anchor: والباقون: نعمة منونة على الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mithqāl is an equivalent weight, from th-q-l, and in “weight of an atom” means its weight; the cited poetry uses mithqāl in the sense of a weight.
rows.anchor: مثقال ذرة، أي: زنته وثقله، قال الشاعر: وكلا نوافيه الجزاء بمثقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm is firm commitment and preparing oneself to do something; fakhara is recounting one's merits, while ikhtiyāl is swaggering pride.
rows.anchor: والعزم: العقد على الأمر، وتوطين النفس على فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghadd means reducing: lowering the gaze diminishes sight and lowering the voice reduces its loudness.
rows.anchor: وغض بصره: إذا نقص النظر، وغض صوته: إذا نقص جهارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “innahā” is explained either as an emphatic or anticipatory pronoun awaiting the clause that interprets it.
rows.anchor: الأول: أنها عماد الضمير على شريطة التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ādhā is an injurious act or word, while baraʾah is becoming clear of something, including illness or debt; wajīh is a person of standing.
rows.anchor: الأذى: ما يؤذي غيره من فعل أو قول يكرهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound statement is free of lies and futile talk; sādīd is sound and free of defect.
rows.anchor: والقول السديد: لا يشوبه كذب ولغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amānah is a binding contract that must be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: والأمانة: عقد يجب الوفاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning not to harm the Messenger is followed by the story of those who harmed Moses to console Muhammad, then the command to speak rightly as believers do.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم النهي عن إيذاء الرسول عقبه بذكر من آذى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Israelites accused Moses of concealing himself because of leprosy or another defect; God publicly cleared him of that slander.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: ما يتستر هذا التستر إلا من عيب برص أو نحوه

rows.speaker: علي وأبو علي
rows.claim: They said Moses killed Aaron, but God restored Aaron to life to tell them Moses had not killed him; Abū ʿAlī chooses this account.
rows.anchor: أشاعوا أن هارون قتله موسى فأحيا الله هارون حتى أخبرهم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliyah reports that Qārūn hired a prostitute to accuse Moses publicly; God protected Moses, she admitted lying, and Qārūn perished.
rows.anchor: استأجر قارون مومسة لتقذف موسى بنفسها على رؤوس الملأ

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says they slandered Moses as a magician, madman, and liar after seeing his signs, as unbelievers habitually do to prophets.
rows.anchor: آذوه من حيث نسبوه إلى السحر والجنون والكذب بعدما رأوا الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that Israelites accused Moses of a genital deformity is unsound because its story exposes nakedness and causes aversion.
rows.anchor: فليس بصحيح [1]؛ لأن فيه هتك الستر، وكشف العورة، وما يؤدي إلى التنفير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: “Sound speech” means correct speech according to Ibn ʿAbbās and just speech according to Qatādah.
rows.anchor: قيل: صوابا، عن ابن عباس. وقيل: عدلا، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers fulfill the trust and merit mercy; God forgives the repentant and shows mercy to believers.
rows.anchor: وأما المؤمن والمؤمنة فأديا الأمانة، واستوجبا الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse prohibits harming prophets, which is unquestionably disbelief.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على المنع من أذى الأنبياء، ولا شبهة أن ذلك كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It prohibits what is unlawful, urges sound speech, and teaches that victory comes through obedience to God and following His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الفوز ينال بطاعة الله، واتباع رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels do not disobey; disobedience is characteristic of humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الملائكة لم تعص وأن العصيان عادة الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The presentation of the trust to the heavens and earth is figurative or addressed to their inhabitants; literal presentation to inanimate things is impossible.
rows.anchor: المراد بالعرض على أهلها أو التمثيل، فأما العرض على الجماد فمحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The presentation describes the state and obligation, not a free choice: God obligates a servant when it is beneficial, without coercing him.
rows.anchor: وقد بينا أنه بيان الحال والتكليف، فأما التخيير فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They refused to carry it” cannot mean meritorious refusal of God's command, which would be disbelief; the author instead says they betrayed the trust while bearing its burden.
rows.anchor: المراد خانوا فيها إذ حملوا وزرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the offer was a choice and the heavens asked for relief from the threat; the author's earlier account is preferable because human welfare is not left to their choice.
rows.anchor: وما قدمناه أولى؛ لأن المصالح لا تقف على اختيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human speech, deeds, sins, carrying the trust, hypocrisy, disbelief, and faith are people's own acts rather than God's creation, making commands, prohibitions, promise, and threat coherent.
rows.anchor: ليصح الأمر والنهي، والوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unanswered “is one who is devout …?” is completed as a comparison with someone enjoying disbelief, whose end is the Fire.
rows.anchor: أمن هو قانت كمن يتمتع بكفره، ثم مصيره إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do good in this world receive a good reward in the afterlife: abiding in Paradise.
rows.anchor: من أحسن العمل في الدنيا فله مثوبة حسنة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥsān can mean generosity toward others and inviting them to religion, or doing what is good by obeying God's commands.
rows.anchor: إحسان إلى الغير بالإنعام عليه والدعاء إلى الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly good may be praise and kind words, while the afterlife good is abundant reward; alternatives define it as goodness (Muqātil) or health and well-being (al-Suddī).
rows.anchor: حسنة في الدنيا بالثناء والمدح والقول الجميل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: God's spacious earth means the worldly earth, so believers should migrate from the land of polytheism.
rows.anchor: الدنيا واسعة، فتهاجروا عن دار الشرك، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مقاتل وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the spacious land as Paradise, to be sought through righteous deeds; another encourages moving to the many fruitful lands promised to them.
rows.anchor: أرض الجنة واسعة فاطلبوها بالأعمال الصالحة، عن مقاتل، وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience may mean enduring migration and exile, obeying and avoiding sin, or bearing afflictions and trials.
rows.anchor: قيل: على الهجرة وترك الوطن والإقامة بالغربة، وقيل: على الطاعة وعن المعصية

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The patient receive reward beyond the measure of their deeds.
rows.anchor: لأنه يعطي أكثر من مقادير الأعمال، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Alternatively, “without reckoning” means without constriction, since a measured reward would be restricted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا [تضييق] فيه؛ لأن ما يعطى بحساب يتضيق، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah emphatically says there is no measuring vessel or scale there.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: لا، والله ما هناك مكيال، ولا ميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies complete divine power and knowledge, perception without instruments, that God does not will evil or punish without guilt, and encouragement of knowledge, migration, and obedience.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على أحكام: منها: كمال قدرته وعلمه. وأنه مدرك لا بآلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creation and shaping in the womb, and the creation of Adam from soil and Eve from Adam's rib, demonstrate perfect power and knowledge; perception through an instrument could not operate in the womb.
rows.anchor: أما الأول: فخلقه وتصويره في الرحم، وخلق آدم من تراب، وخلق حواء من ضلعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statements that God does not approve disbelief for His servants, accepts gratitude, and does not let one soul bear another's burden refute attribution of wrongful conduct to Him.
rows.anchor: الكفر)، وقوله: (وإن تشكروا يرضه لكم).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses about people's own deeds and their return to God, including the case of a person struck by hardship, condemn bad human conduct and show that it is theirs.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون)، وقوله: (وإذا مس الإنسان) الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: References to the devout person, hope for mercy, reflection, idolaters, misleading others, and fearing God refute the claim that human acts are created in people by God.
rows.anchor: قوله: (أمن هو قانت)، وقوله: (ويرجو رحمة ربه)، وقوله: (إنما يتذكر)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation to worship at night shows that night vigil is better than daytime worship because the heart is less distracted and ostentation less likely.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (آناء الليل) أن قيام الليل أفضل من قيام النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer should worship God between fear and hope, as expressed by hoping for His mercy.
rows.anchor: قوله: (ويرجو رحمة ربه) أن المؤمن يجب أن يعبد ربه بين الخوف والرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good-doer is repaid with good; this depends on the doctrine that people act and God rewards the good-doer for good and the evildoer for evil.
rows.anchor: أن المحسن يجازى بالإحسان، وجميع ذلك إنما يصح على مذهب العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn die like humans, as indicated by the word “passed away.”
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الجن يموتون كالإنس؛ لذلك قال: خلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse saying “that is the recompense” shows punishment is deserved on account of deeds.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ذلك جزآء) أن العقاب يستحق على الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The misguidance mentioned in “our Lord” comes from humans and jinn, not God; if God created their disbelief, their misleading others would have no effect.
rows.anchor: الإضلال من الإنس والجن، خلاف ما تقوله المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage teaches following evidence rather than leaders.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب اتباع الدليل دون الرؤساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final statement implies that the punishment of the people of Hell differs by degree according to their deserved punishment.
rows.anchor: عذاب أهل النار يتفاضل على قدر الاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiqāmah is continuing along a straight path; a walī is a close ally who supports another, and ḥamīm is an intimate protector.
rows.anchor: الاستقامة: الاستمرار على الطريقة المستقيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzul can mean benefit or gift, a host's prepared hospitality, or the food offered as hospitality.
rows.anchor: والنزل: ما يقيمه لضيفه إكراما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb tadʿūna derives from an iftiʿāl form of daʿaw, with metathesis and assimilation yielding its present form.
rows.anchor: تدعون: افتعال من دعوت ادعى، يدعي ادعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “nor” either strengthens the negation as a poetic pleonasm or emphasizes that neither side equals the other.
rows.anchor: وفي تكرير (لا) في قوله: (ولا السيئة) قولان

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt for each wind that has blown in the world.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة (الذاريات) أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد كل ريح هبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Qāf closes with the threat of punishment and a command to be patient, this surah opens by swearing that the promised judgment is true and will arrive.
rows.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (ق) بالوعيد افتتح هذه السورة بالقسم بأن ما توعدون حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhāriyāt is wind that scatters and lifts dust, usually a moderate wind; stronger winds are called ʿāṣifah and then qāṣifah as they increase and break things.
rows.anchor: وهو من ذرت الريح التراب تذروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaml with fatḥa means a load in the womb or on a tree, while ḥiml with kasra is what one carries on one's back; the cited poem witnesses “ḥāmilah” for a pregnant woman.
rows.anchor: والحمل بالفتح: ما كان في بطن أو على رأس شجرة، وبالكسر: ما حملته على ظهرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman may be called ḥāmil because it is an adjective used only of females, like ṭāliq and ḥāʾiḍ; another explanation is that it means “possessor of pregnancy.”
rows.anchor: ويقال: امرأة حامل؛ لأنه نعت لا يكون إلا للمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wiqr with kasra means a load; a heavily laden date palm is muwqir because its burden weighs on it, from the root for heaviness.
rows.anchor: والوقر بكسر الواو: الحمل، يقال: نخلة موقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāriyāt is the plural of jāriyah and derives from the verb to run; dīn may mean recompense, religion, reckoning, or custom.
rows.anchor: والجاريات: جمع جارية، وأصله من جرى يجري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥubuk can mean beauty and evenness of workmanship, fine weaving, tracks or paths, a tightly formed construction, or a pattern such as stripes in a garment.
rows.anchor: والحبك: حسن أثر الصنعة في الشيء واستواؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds and clouds display God's great power and blessings, making them fit subjects for an oath.
rows.anchor: تدل الآيات على عظيم قدرته تعالى في الرياح والسحاب وما فيها من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses affirm that recompense for actions will occur, contrary to the Jabriyya.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وقوع الجزاء على الأعمال، خلاف قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The act of making baseless guesses is a human act.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الخرص فعل العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description “in a flood, heedless” shows that knowledge is acquired.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (في غمرة ساهون) أن المعارف مكتسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narratives of earlier communities provide lessons for anyone who reflects; this is why they are recounted.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن في قصصهم عبرة لمن تدبر، وأنه إنما ذكر ليعتبر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayd means strength; yad also means power, dominance, or emphasis in Arabic, but not an attribute inhering in the divine essence as the Kullābiyya claim.
rows.anchor: واليد: الجارحة المعروفة، واليد: القوة، واليد تذكر، ويراد الغلبة والتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kullābī claim about a divine attribute called “hand” fails conceptually because the claim is unintelligible and cannot be established either immediately or by inference.
rows.anchor: وما قالوه غير معقول، ولأن الشيء إما أن يعلم ضرورة أو استدلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim also fails linguistically: Arabic does not use “hand” to mean an attribute.
rows.anchor: ليس في كلام العرب اليد بمعنى الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īsāʿ means broadening or making space across the possible directions, and mūsiʿ is one who makes spacious.
rows.anchor: والإيساع: الإكثار من الذهاب في الجهات بما يمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farsh may mean the act or object spread out, ground-hugging livestock or birds, a spouse, a laid carpet, or vegetation that lies on the ground without a stalk.
rows.anchor: والفرش: مصدر فرشت، والفرش: المفروش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mahd is a prepared place of rest, and the related verbs mean preparing or making a place suitable for settling.
rows.anchor: والمهد: الموضع المهيأ للاستقرار عليه

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises an easy reckoning from God for anyone who recites Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة (الحاقة) حاسبه الله حسابا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Resurrection warning in al-Qalam and the command to endure the unbelievers' abuse, al-Ḥāqqah opens with the Resurrection and its events.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر في سورة (القلم) حديث القيامة ووعيد الكفار،

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read “min maʿahum” with kasra on qāf and fatḥa on bāʾ, meaning followers and troops accompanying a person; this is also reported from al-Ḥasan and al-Sulamī and narrated from ʿĀṣim.
rows.anchor: ومن قبلهم بكسر القاف وفتح الباء، وهو قراءة الحسن والسلمي واختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers say “before him,” referring to earlier peoples; the “with him” reading is supported by readings attributed to Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون: ومن قبله بفتح القاف وسكون الباء، أي: من تقدمه من الأمم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the singular “the overturned city” without the alif, whereas the common reading is plural.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: والمؤتفكات بالألف على الجمع، وعن الحسن: المؤتفكة بغير ألف

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: One explanation calls al-Ḥāqqah a name for the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: إنه اسم من أسماء القيامة، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Another derives it from “truth”: God's promise and threat become true at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: لأن وعده ووعيده يحق فيها، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it is so called because the realities of deeds become clear there.
rows.anchor: لأنه يتبين فيها حقائق الأعمال فسميت الحاقة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: It can mean the inevitable event, when each person necessarily receives recompense for his deeds.
rows.anchor: الحاقة: الواجبة، من قولهم: حق، أي: وجب

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī calls it the Day of truth; other explanations say it is a true event with no denial or a day that overpowers the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سميت الحاقة؛ لأنها يوم الحق، عن الكسائي

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the chapter was revealed in Medina.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا فذكر الحسن، والضحاك أنها نزلت بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports place its revelation between Mecca and Medina, in Mecca, or upon the Prophet's first arrival in Medina, respectively attributed to a group, Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Farrāʾ.
rows.anchor: وذكر جماعة أنها نزلت بين مكة والمدينة.

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the sealed nectar to anyone who recites Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة (المطففين) سقاه الله من الرحيق المختوم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah develops the preceding al-Infiṭār ending, which mentioned Resurrection and the fates of the righteous and wicked, by detailing people's conditions at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (انفطرت) بذكر القيامة، وما أعد للأبرار والفجار

rows.speaker: عامة القراء
rows.claim: The common reading joins “they measure for them” as a transitive construction, with “them” as the object; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar instead pauses after “they measure” and starts “they are defrauders” with “they” as subject, a reading attributed to Ḥamzah.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: (كالوهم أو وزنوهم) متصلا بغير ألف، ولا وقف بين (كالوا)، وبين (هم).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the joined reading because the written form lacks an alif, Arabic says “I measured your due” meaning “for you,” and the readers unanimously use it.
rows.anchor: والأوجه الأول لوجوه: أحدها: أنهم كتبوها بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭafīf means tiny or insignificant; a mutaffif reduces another person's proper measure or weight, whether by a small shortfall or a subtle theft.
rows.anchor: الطفيف: الشيء التفه القليل، والمطفف: المقلل حق صاحبه بنقصانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation names the act for the tiny amount missing from the rightful measure.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأن ما ينقص منه طفيف قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view calls the act a secret theft of a small amount.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التطفيف: أن يسرق الشيء اليسير في خفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Related usage describes an underfilled vessel and says all descendants of Adam are close to a full measure.
rows.anchor: وإناء طفان إذا لم يكن ملآن، ومنه: بنو آدم كلهم طف الصاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one has superiority over another except through piety.
rows.anchor: فليس لأحد على أحد فضل إلا بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful; the verb describes ingratitude for a blessing. The tribe Kinda is named from separation after a son rebelled against his father.
rows.anchor: ومنه سمي : كندة ؛ لأنه كند أباه ففارقه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī gives dialectal meanings: disobedient in Kinda, stingy among Banū Mālik, and ungrateful among Muḍar and Rabīʿah.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي : الكنود بلسان كندة : العاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse singles out ingratitude to God: failing to thank a human benefactor is easier because the benefit is near, and even the greatest human gift, parents, is slight beside God's smallest gift.
rows.anchor: لأن أجل ما أنعم به على الإنسان من مثله نعمة أبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse “his mother fell” is said over a doomed man: as he falls and perishes, his mother falls into bereavement and grief; the verse means the person whose scales are light has perished.
rows.anchor: من قولهم إذا دعوا على الرجل بالهلكة : هوت أمّه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Hāwiyah is a name for Hell, a deep fire into which its people plunge; a report says one falls in it for seventy years, so it is their abode.
rows.anchor: من أسماء النار ، وكأنها النار العميقة لهوي أهل النار فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abode may be called a mother by analogy because a mother is a child's refuge and place of shelter.
rows.anchor: للمأوى : أمّ ، على التشبيه ؛ لأنّ الأمّ مأوى الولد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah says the person's head, his “mother,” falls to the bottom of Hell because he is cast into it headfirst.
rows.anchor: فأمّ رأسه هاوية في قعر جهنم ؛ لأنه يطرح فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It” may refer to the calamity implied by the first interpretation or to Hāwiyah; the final hāʾ is a pausal letter, which some drop in connected recitation while others retain, as in the written codex.
rows.anchor: والهاء للسكت ، وإذا وصل القارىء حذفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone loses in trade except the righteous, who buy the afterlife with the world and gain happiness; all who trade in the opposite way lose and suffer.
rows.anchor: أن الناس في خسران من تجارتهم إلا الصالحين وحدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq is what is established and may not rightly be denied, encompassing all goodness: monotheism, obedience, following scripture and messengers, and preferring the afterlife over the world.
rows.anchor: بالأمر الثابت الذي لا يسوغ إنكاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience means refraining from sins, maintaining obedience, and enduring whatever God uses to test His servants.
rows.anchor: عن المعاصي وعلى الطاعات ، على ما يبلو الله به عباده

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says reciting Sūrat al-ʿAṣr brings God's forgiveness and places the reciter among those who urge one another to truth and patience.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة ( والعصر ) غفر الله له
